conflicts.permit: We use Sensitive Personal Information from other Consumers (including racial or ethnic origin, religious beliefs, mental or physical health diagnosis, sexual orientation, or citizenship or immigration status) to provide disability accommodations.
conflicts.prohibit: sensitive personal information (collected only about employees or vendors; or precise geolocation of consenting users)
conflicts.situation: NewsBreak collects and uses health or other sensitive information from a consumer who is neither an employee nor a vendor to provide a disability accommodation.
conflicts.reason: The category list limits sensitive personal information to employees, vendors, and consenting users' precise geolocation, yet the policy also uses such data from other consumers. No exception or precedence statement reconciles the two.

conflicts.permit: If you register for an account with us, you provide us your account name, email address, password.
conflicts.prohibit: sensitive personal information (collected only about employees or vendors; or precise geolocation of consenting users)
conflicts.situation: A consumer registers a NewsBreak account and provides an account name and password, which the policy lists as account log-in sensitive personal information.
conflicts.reason: The policy defines account log-in as sensitive personal information and says such information is collected only about employees or vendors or as precise geolocation. Account registration collects it from ordinary users with no stated exception.

conflicts.permit: You might choose to provide your birth year or gender.
conflicts.prohibit: sensitive personal information (collected only about employees or vendors; or precise geolocation of consenting users)
conflicts.situation: A registered NewsBreak user chooses to provide gender, which the policy lists as sensitive personal information.
conflicts.reason: Gender appears in the policy's list of sensitive personal information, which the policy says is collected only about employees or vendors or as precise geolocation. Optional gender collection from users is not carved out.

conflicts.permit: These third parties have access to your Personal Data only to perform these tasks on our behalf and are obligated not to disclose or use it for any other purpose.
conflicts.prohibit: RealDating will not sell or rent any client data loaded into our system and only the registered account holder and our support staff can gain access to the uploaded data.
conflicts.situation: A user's uploaded profile data, such as name and email, is processed by a RealDating service provider that hosts or analyzes the service.
conflicts.reason: One statement limits access to uploaded data to the account holder and support staff, while the addendum gives service providers access to Personal Data. The policy states no exception or precedence between the original policy and addendum.

conflicts.permit: Google may use the collected data to contextualize and personalize the ads of its own advertising network.
conflicts.prohibit: These third parties have access to your Personal Data only to perform these tasks on our behalf and are obligated not to disclose or use it for any other purpose.
conflicts.situation: Google Analytics, engaged as a service provider, collects usage data such as IP address and device identifiers from the app and uses it for Google's advertising network.
conflicts.reason: Service providers are said to use Personal Data only on RealDating's behalf, but Google, listed as an analytics service provider, may use collected data for its own ads. The policy does not say which governs.

conflicts.permit: Usage Data is generally retained for a shorter period of time, except when this data is used to strengthen the security or to improve the functionality of our Service, or we are legally obligated to retain this data for longer time periods.
conflicts.prohibit: We only use this information for statistical analysis purposes and then the data is removed from the system.
conflicts.situation: Page-visit data collected through traffic log cookies is kept and used to strengthen security or improve functionality of the app.
conflicts.reason: The cookie section limits traffic log data to statistical analysis followed by removal, while the addendum allows longer retention of Usage Data, including pages visited, for security and functionality. No precedence is stated.

conflicts.permit: RealDating may disclose your Personal Data in the good faith belief that such action is necessary to:
conflicts.prohibit: We will not sell, distribute or lease your personal information to third parties unless we have your permission or are required by law to do so.
conflicts.situation: RealDating discloses a user's personal data to a third party to defend its own rights or property, without the user's permission and without a legal requirement.
conflicts.reason: The prohibition allows disclosure only with permission or when required by law, but the legal requirements section permits disclosure on a good faith belief to protect RealDating's rights. Neither statement names the other as an exception.

conflicts.permit: The information we collect about you may be used to improve the relevancy of our marketing
conflicts.prohibit: We will not process your information for the purposes of targeted marketing or pass your information on to third parties for the purposes of such marketing unless you give your consent or you have given it already.
conflicts.situation: Soccer Manager uses a player's collected information to build lookalike audiences for marketing to potential new users, without the player having given marketing consent.
conflicts.reason: Lookalike processing is stated under legitimate interests with an opt-out, while targeted marketing requires consent. The policy does not say whether lookalike audience creation counts as targeted marketing.

conflicts.permit: However, the app may use third party code and libraries that use “cookies” to collect information and improve their services.
conflicts.prohibit: However, they are obligated not to disclose or use the information for any other purpose.
conflicts.situation: A third party library such as Google Play Services collects app user information through cookies and uses it to improve its own services.
conflicts.reason: Third parties are said to use information only for tasks on the developer's behalf, yet third party code may use collected information to improve their own services. The policy does not reconcile the two.

conflicts.permit: I want to inform you that whenever you use my Service, in a case of an error in the app I collect data and information (through third party products) on your phone called Log Data.
conflicts.prohibit: The information that I request will be retained on your device and is not collected by me in any way.
conflicts.situation: When the app errors, the developer collects Log Data, including the device IP address and device name, through third party products.
conflicts.reason: One statement says requested information stays on the device and is never collected, while another says the developer collects Log Data with identifying details. The policy does not clearly separate requested information from Log Data.

conflicts.permit: If you contact us via our support channel, we will store your message(s) and other information you choose to give us (for example error logs or information related to your mobile device or your store account) for further analysis.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not collect any personal information about our players, users or our website visitors.
conflicts.situation: A player contacts Secret Exit support and provides messages, store account details, or device information, which the company stores for analysis.
conflicts.reason: The policy states it collects no personal information about players, yet it stores support messages and account information and later refers to private information collected via the support channel. No exception is stated.

conflicts.permit: If you contact us via our support channel, we will store your message(s) and other information you choose to give us (for example error logs or information related to your mobile device or your store account) for further analysis.
conflicts.prohibit: None of your personal information is stored on our servers.
conflicts.situation: A player's support message containing store account or device details is stored by Secret Exit for further analysis.
conflicts.reason: The policy says no personal information is stored on its servers, but it stores support messages and account details without saying where they are kept or excluding them.

conflicts.permit: Facebook will share with Us, based on the Facebook privacy policy, the information available on your Facebook account, including, without limitation, your profile information, friends’ names, photos, privacy settings and certain other information that will be explained to you (and authorized by you) during the App’s log-in process.
conflicts.prohibit: Currently, Web sites and Apps do not collect Personal Information.
conflicts.situation: A user logs in to an app with Facebook, and Facebook shares profile information, friends' names, and photos with the app operator.
conflicts.reason: The policy says its apps collect no Personal Information, defined to include names, yet it receives Facebook profile information and friends' names at log-in. The policy gives no exception for social log-in.

conflicts.permit: Our Apps will collect precise information about the location of your mobile device, but you can opt-out by changing the settings on your mobile device.
conflicts.prohibit: Currently, Web sites and Apps do not collect Personal Information.
conflicts.situation: An app user with default location settings has the device's precise location collected by the app.
conflicts.reason: Precise device location can identify an individual, yet the policy says apps collect no Personal Information. The definition lists examples without saying whether precise location is included or excluded.

conflicts.permit: You can sign into your account to see or delete any personally identifiable information we have stored, such as your name, address, email or phone number.
conflicts.prohibit: In other words, we do not collect information such as your name, address, phone number or email address.
conflicts.situation: A registered user's account holds a name, address, email, or phone number that VAPP has stored.
conflicts.reason: The policy says VAPP does not collect names, addresses, phone numbers, or emails, yet describes stored identifiable information of exactly these types in user accounts. No exception separates the statements.

conflicts.permit: We may share personally identifiable information (such as name, address, email or phone) with trusted partners in order to provide you with relevant advertising, offers or services.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not collect personally identifiable information about you.
conflicts.situation: VAPP shares a user's name, email, or phone number with trusted partners for advertising or offers.
conflicts.reason: Sharing identifiable information with partners requires VAPP to hold it, but the policy says it collects no personally identifiable information. Neither statement limits the other.

conflicts.permit: To operate the service, we also may make identifiable and anonymous information available to third parties in these limited circumstances
conflicts.prohibit: We only share this location information with others as approved by you.
conflicts.situation: VAPP discloses a user's stored precise location to a purchaser in an asset sale or to protect its rights, without the user's approval.
conflicts.reason: The location statement allows sharing only with user approval, while the disclosure section lists cases where consent is not required. The policy does not say whether location data falls under those cases.
